subject: qe-plan
reason: Split into 4 AppHost unit cases, 5 migration/seed functional cases, a health case, 9 /active cases (filter, order, tie-break, fields, empty, both boundaries, token handling), 5 authenticated list cases (200, 3x 401, e2e sign-in scope) and 2 Identity scope cases.

items.title: promotions-api references and waits for eventbus and promotionsdb
items.reason: The scaffold's core wiring (own DB, event bus) must hold; WaitFor controls startup order, which the story says to check on the model rather than by timing. Unit layer per Test scope.

items.title: promotions-api has an HTTP health check on /health
items.reason: The Aspire dashboard shows the service healthy only if the health check annotation points at `/health`; a wrong path would leave it Unhealthy forever. Unit layer per Test scope.

items.title: promotions-api gets the Identity__Url environment variable
items.reason: AddDefaultAuthentication reads `Identity:Url` to validate tokens; without the variable `GET /api/promotions` could never return 200 under Aspire. Unit layer per Test scope.

items.title: webapp and ordering-api reference promotions-api
items.reason: Other teams build on Promotions from Day 1 through these references; `orderingApi` is declared before `promotionsApi`, so a missed or misordered statement is a real risk. Unit layer per Test scope.

items.title: Startup migration creates the five tables on an empty database
items.reason: The migration is the first thing every later promotion story depends on; checking `information_schema` is the cheapest way to prove all five tables, including the shared `IntegrationEventLog`, exist. Functional layer per Test scope (real Postgres).

items.title: Seeder inserts exactly the four seeded promotions
covers: AC: seed data matches the table
items.reason: The seed table has per-row requirements (rule type, coupon-only, status, window); a single case asserts each row so a wrong type or window fails with a precise diff.

items.title: Seeder inserts coupons FALL10 and WELCOME5 on the coupon-only promotion
items.reason: Later stories (PROMO-4) rely on these codes belonging to the coupon-only promotion; separate from the promotion rows because it exercises the foreign key and the empty redemption table.

items.title: Restarting against the same database keeps 4 promotions and 2 coupons
covers: AC: starts again against the same database
items.reason: Aspire restarts the service routinely; a seeder that appended on every start would duplicate promotions and double-count them in `/active`.

items.title: Seeder inserts nothing when Promotions already has a row
covers: Outputs: if the Promotions table already has any row, the seeder inserts nothing
items.reason: Distinct from a plain restart: here the existing row is not seed data, so it proves the guard checks any row, not a count of 4.

items.title: /health and /alive return 200 when the database is reachable
items.reason: Aspire's health check and readiness depend on these endpoints; checked at the functional layer because it needs the real service and database.

items.title: GET /active returns the four seeded promotions and no inactive ones
covers: Outputs: coupon-only promotions count as active
items.reason: Core filter rule: Published and inside the window. The three extras each break one condition (status, end, start), so a filter that drops any one condition fails here.

items.title: GET /active orders promotions by priority descending
items.reason: Order is part of the contract that PROMO-3 consumes; split from the filter case so an ordering bug does not hide behind a membership assertion.

items.title: Promotions with equal priority are ordered by id ascending
items.reason: The seeded priorities are all distinct, so the tie-break needs its own data; without it the order is nondeterministic across runs.

items.title: Each active promotion has the required fields
covers: Outputs: each element has id, name, type, status, startsAt, endsAt, priority, requiresCoupon
items.reason: PROMO-2 owns the final shape, but the story fixes this minimum; checking values rather than presence catches a type/status serialized as a number.

items.title: GET /active returns 200 and an empty array when nothing is active
covers: Outputs: when no promotion is active it returns 200 with []
items.reason: An empty result must not be 404 or null; callers iterate the body.

items.title: A promotion with StartsAt equal to now is active
items.reason: Lower boundary of the window; an off-by-one (`<`) would hide a promotion at the instant it starts. Uses a fake `TimeProvider` so the instant is exact.

items.title: A promotion with EndsAt equal to now is not active
items.reason: Upper boundary is exclusive; an off-by-one (`<=`) would keep applying a promotion after it ended. Uses a fake `TimeProvider`.

items.title: GET /active ignores a malformed bearer token
covers: Outputs: ignores any bearer token sent with it
AC: malformed bearer token still returns 200
items.reason: Anonymous endpoints can still fail with 401 when the auth middleware validates a bad token first; this protects anonymous callers whose client sends a stale header.

items.title: GET /active returns the same result with a valid token
covers: Outputs: ignores any bearer token sent with it
items.reason: Confirms a valid token neither changes the result nor causes per-user filtering.

items.title: GET /api/promotions with a promotions-scope token returns every promotion
covers: Outputs: GET /api/promotions returns 200 with every promotion, active or not
items.reason: Distinguishes the admin-style list from `/active`: inactive rows must be included. Functional layer because the token is validated against a real Identity.

items.title: Signing in to the WebApp yields a token with the promotions scope that is accepted
covers: AC: user signs in to the WebApp
Outputs: WebApp requests the promotions scope at sign-in
items.reason: Only the real WebApp sign-in proves the WebApp requests the scope and the webapp client is allowed it; no cheaper layer exercises both sides. Test stack scenario must load promotions data because the stack runs with `Seeding__Disabled=true`.

items.title: GET /api/promotions without a token returns 401
items.reason: Protects the temporary list endpoint from anonymous access.

items.title: GET /api/promotions with a malformed token returns 401
items.reason: A garbage token must be rejected, not treated as anonymous; separate from the missing-token case because the validation path differs.

items.title: GET /api/promotions with an expired token returns 401
items.reason: Lifetime validation is a separate failure from format validation.

items.title: Identity discovery document lists the promotions scope
covers: Outputs: Identity has an API resource and an API scope named promotions
items.reason: Cheapest observable proof that the `ApiScope` and `ApiResource` are registered in Identity.API.

items.title: Other clients cannot request the promotions scope
covers: Outputs: promotions is in the webapp client's allowed scopes only
items.reason: The story decided the scope goes to `webapp` only; this catches it being added to another client.

reason: 24 of 26 cases are faithfully implemented with exact assertions against real systems. TC-PROMO-1-21 never uses the WebApp's own token (it parses the Identity log and fetches a separate token), and TC-PROMO-1-02 checks the /health path only through the annotation key.

items.reason: The case requires reading the access token the WebApp holds for the session, decoding its scope claim and calling the API with it. The test reads the requested scope from the Identity container log (first match, fragile), then obtains a separate token for alice via getTokens and asserts on that token. This does not show that the WebApp session holds a token with the promotions scope. The sign-in check is only that the 'Sign in' label is absent, not that alice is shown as signed in.

reason: All 26 cases are covered and 25 follow their steps and exact expected values on real Postgres and Identity; TC-21 deviates because it asserts the scope and calls Promotions.API with a separately minted token instead of the one the WebApp holds. I did not open the TC-21 keyframes.

items.reason: The case requires reading the access token the WebApp holds, decoding its scope claim and calling GET /api/promotions with that token. subject: implementer
reason: Fixes 21 bugs found by the test stack flow mapping across Ordering.API (ownership, identity, error mapping), Catalog.API (write auth, validation, paging), Identity/ServiceDefaults (token audience), WebApp (open redirect, missing-product basket, page clamp, cart JS race), Basket.API (quantity validation) and Webhooks.API (event name validation). Tickets ship as 9 PR groups by service and root cause; security fixes are kept apart from the easy fixes. A shared admin role in Identity.API (owned by BUG-4) is the one cross-group contract: BUG-2 (ship only for admins) depends on it, and BUG-6 follows BUG-4 because both change Identity Config.cs.

items.reason: Filter GetOrderAsync by buyers.IdentityGuid from IIdentityService and return 404. Owns the order visibility rule that BUG-2 reuses.
Cancel: ownership check, 404 for orders the caller can't see. Ship: RequireRole Admin using BUG-4's role claim. Leave mapping OrderingDomainException to 409 to BUG-10.
Take the buyer id and name from IIdentityService. Leave the 200-on-failure behaviour to BUG-9.

Owns the Admin role and catalog scope contracts. Change only the endpoint mapping lines (100-115) in CatalogApi.cs; validation belongs to the catalog-validation tickets. Wire the Identity reference for Catalog in AppHost and run testing/teststack publish.
Accept only local paths (a single '/' not followed by '/' or '\'); otherwise '/'.

Attach every ApiScope (including BUG-4's catalog) to its ApiResource and turn on audience validation. Check that the WebApp, webhook client and mobile BFF still request every scope they call. Do not touch the role contract.
Use TryGetValue and skip lines whose product is missing.
Validate with BasketItem.Validate and throw RpcException InvalidArgument before saving.
Return a 400 ValidationProblem when CreateOrder fails validation, following BUG-10's error mapping.
Map OrderingDomainException to 409 and keep BUG-2's 404 for missing or other buyers' orders.
Range-check PaginationRequest; do not touch the write endpoints.
Clamp Page to at least 1 before calling the catalog service.
Add the empty-name and negative-price rules to BUG-17's validator.
Mark the input committed (or blur it) on Enter, and ignore change events while a submit is in flight.
A null or empty draft body returns 400 through the same ValidationProblem shape.
Require Enum.IsDefined after TryParse. Check which flows file lists the webhooks bug row.

Existing id on create: 409 (or ignore the client id).
Check that the brand and type exist in the shared validator; return 400 naming the id.
